newsitem.title: USA: Americans warned of criminal threat in Bahamas.
newsitem.headline: Americans warned of criminal threat in Bahamas.

text.p: The U.S. State Department said on Friday it had information that criminals in the Bahamas might be planning to attack U.S. interests there, and urged American citizens on the islands to take care.
A public announcement said the U.S. embassy in the capital Nassau "has received information that local criminal elements may be planning unspecified violence against U.S. interests in the Bahamas".
Bahamian and U.S. authorities were investigating the information, the announcement said.

The U.S. embassy urged American citizens to pay extra attention to their security, "maintain awareness of their surroundings" while in the Bahamas, and report suspicious activity to local authorities, it said.
The announcement did not identify the criminal elements or explain why U.S. interests might be targeted.

The Bahamas, home to about 254,000 people, is a chain of hundreds of islands in the Atlantic Ocean east of Florida and the Caribbean. In recent years it has been attempting to shed a reputation as a drug transit nation.
At a news briefing, State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns sought to play down concern over the warning.
"I don't think there's any cause for public hysteria concerning this announcement. We're certainly not recommending that American citizens leave the Bahamas," he said.
Burns refused to give further information on the threat "because that might give an advantage to the criminals themselves".
